description:
The cluster bootstrap record names the tag-0 materializers recovery must
look up (bedrock-q67.21.12). It is written ONLY by recovery. The
`materializers/0/*` keyspace family names the same members and is
written by BOTH recovery and the distributor, whose startup sweep treats
tag 0 like any other tag: it verifies, adopts, heals, recruits, and
RETIRES.

Retirement is the hazard. Sequence, all healthy behaviour:

1. Recovery records pointer = {w1}, keyspace = {w1}.
2. The distributor recruits w2 for tag 0. keyspace = {w1, w2}.
3. w1 dies. The distributor heals: keyspace = {w2}. Pointer still {w1}.
4. Recovery runs. It reads the pointer, finds only w1, w1 is gone ->
   {:system_materializers_unavailable, %{"w1" => ...}}. Stall.

A healthy w2 is sitting right there and recovery cannot see it, because
reading the keyspace requires a serving tag-0 materializer and finding
one requires the pointer. The union of pointer and keyspace does not
help: the keyspace is unreadable precisely when it would matter.

This is NOT introduced by bedrock-q67.21.13 — that ticket removed
recovery's DATA-tag management and left tag 0 exactly as it was. The
hazard is present today.

WHAT FDB DOES: the set of servers holding recovery-bootstrap metadata
changes only during recovery. cstate names the tlogs; losing a tlog
triggers a new recovery, which recruits replacements and rewrites cstate
in the same pass. DD never adds or removes a tlog. FDB also never has
our chicken-and-egg: the txnStateStore lives on the TLOGS, not on a
DD-managed storage shard, so the metadata recovery reads is structurally
outside DD's reach. `\xff/keyServers` exists on regular storage servers
too, but recovery does not read that copy.

Bedrock collapsed those two roles into tag 0: it is both a
materializer-served shard (so distributor-managed) and the store
recovery bootstraps from (so recovery-managed). That collapse is the
actual defect; the retirement race is a symptom.

CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS, none obviously right:

(a) The distributor excludes tag 0 entirely. Clean single ownership, and
    FDB-shaped. Cost: tag 0 gets no healing or elastic membership
    between recoveries, and a tag-0 death has to trigger a recovery.
    Recovery does not recruit tag-0 replicas today, so a fresh cluster
    would have exactly one tag-0 materializer forever, and losing that
    node bricks the cluster until an operator intervenes. Needs
    tag-0 replication-factor recruitment to be worth anything.

(b) The distributor may ADD tag-0 members but never retire them.
    Additions keep pointer as a subset of keyspace, which is the safe
    direction: recovery finds a live named member, then reads the
    keyspace and learns the rest. Retirement stays recovery-only. Cost:
    an asymmetric rule for one tag, and dead tag-0 entries accumulate in
    the keyspace until a recovery prunes them (routing would pick a dead
    ref -- see how RoutingData.pick_member/1 handles it).

(c) The distributor updates the pointer whenever it changes tag-0
    membership. Two records, two stores (object storage and keyspace),
    no atomicity between them. Rejected unless someone finds an ordering
    that makes the crash window safe in both directions.

(d) Give recovery a second copy of the metadata that the distributor
    cannot reach -- the true FDB shape. Largest change; possibly the
    right one.

DECIDE BEFORE: bedrock-q67.21.6 (in-band retirement) and any work that
gives tag 0 a replication factor.

comments.text: GitHub issue: https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/issues/237. Published the 2026-09-05 implementation evaluation, pinned to 8f962e09, with evidence and acceptance criteria. Reproduced findings are distinguished from source-level risks. No implementation fix is included.

Reproduced #237 before production edits with real ShardServer chunk+buffer history, real Olivine workers, and real Distributor fenced add/retire handlers. Epoch2 bootstrap stalls solely on stale CoreState w1 after committed family becomesw2. Regression test bootstrap_membership_test.exs. Proposed authority is existing independent recovered log/chunk record, reconstructing fresh tag0 coverage rather than synchronizing distributor with bootstrap. Cold plan: /tmp/bedrock-issue-team-20260905/237-plan.md; production implementation paused for review.

Cold design review approved (/tmp/bedrock-issue-team-20260905/237-plan-review.md). Amendments accepted: legacy empty/ambiguous hints reconstruct, warm cache must remain named at its node in recovered committed membership, publication tests must preserve actual old/new LOG identities. Two red cases now green with fresh epoch ShardServer durable=nil and only WAL suffix replayed; chunk prefix supplies nondefault layout. Implementing crash/publication and failure-cleanup validation next.

Implemented cold-reviewed independent log/chunk reconstruction with named warm membership validation, legacy fresh rebuild, RV-preserving snapshot replay and cleanup of newly created unpublished failures. Eight real integration regressions cover nil-durable new epoch/chunk-only prefix, stale/displaced workers and actual persistence+failed bootstrap CAS/next-epoch LOG identity. Final validation complete: focused 45 tests,0 failures; Dialyzer zero errors/skips; format/diff checks clean. Awaiting independent final audit before publication.

Independent final audit found downstream data-shard startup failure leaked newly reconstructed tag0 worker. Added four tests: new/warm bootstrap x data lock/unlock failure; two new-worker controls red before fix (237-audit-red.log),49 focused green after cleanup only bootstrap_services creations. Existing warm/data workers preserved. Reviewer rechecking; final quality rerun.

Proceeding authorized commit/push/draft PR.

title: Tag 0 has two membership owners: the distributor can retire the member the durable pointer names
